title: Songs of the Sabbath Sacrifice — Hobah Translation
about: The Songs of the Sabbath Sacrifice are a cycle of thirteen liturgical compositions known from several Qumran Cave 4 manuscripts, a Cave 11 copy, and a manuscript from Masada. The Hebrew fragments describe the heavenly sanctuary, angelic priesthood, divine throne, and ordered praise offered on successive Sabbaths. No single surviving copy preserves the whole cycle continuously.

translation.status: Hobah provisional source-language reading translation of the thirteen-song cycle from surviving fragments
translation.base_text: The Hebrew Songs of the Sabbath Sacrifice tradition represented by 4Q400–407, 11Q17, and the Masada witness, with the different copies used as parallel witnesses rather than silently collapsed
translation.method: Fresh modern-English rendering of recoverable phrases and coherent units. Because the compositions are fragmentary, each song is presented as a readable reconstruction of preserved sense with brackets and ellipses where substantial text is missing.
translation.confidence: Medium in continuous overlapping fragments; low to medium where sequence or restoration depends heavily on reconstruction
translation.notes: The thirteen labels reflect the liturgical cycle. This reader does not imply that the surviving fragments provide thirteen complete songs word-for-word.
translation.license_note: The ancient Hebrew manuscripts are public domain. Hobah English wording is newly prepared for this project.

chapters.label: First Sabbath Song — Priests of the heavenly sanctuary
chapters.text: [For the Instructor.] Praise the God of knowledge, you holy ones appointed to his service. Bless the God of gods, all who stand in the council of holiness. He established the spirits of understanding in their stations and gave the heavenly priests their portions. Their service is without corruption, and their praise rises in the sanctuary of his glory. [Much is missing.]

chapters.label: Second Sabbath Song — The statutes of the holy ones
chapters.text: The holy ones proclaim the statutes by which their ranks are ordered. No rebellion is found in their divisions, and no impurity approaches their service. Each knows the mystery assigned to his station. They bless the King of holiness according to the knowledge he has given them, and their voices answer one another in ordered praise.

chapters.label: Third Sabbath Song — Seven priestly councils
chapters.text: The text speaks of exalted priestly councils and princes of the heavenly priesthood. They serve before the glorious King and teach the mysteries of holiness within their appointed ranks. Blessing passes from one order to another, and the sanctuary is filled with knowledge. [Names and portions of the lists are broken.]

chapters.label: Fourth Sabbath Song — Tongues of knowledge
chapters.text: Wonderful tongues of knowledge praise him, and the sound of blessing comes from those who possess understanding. Their words are not empty noise: each utterance corresponds to the glory revealed to its order. The heavenly assembly recounts God's works, his judgments, and the splendour of his kingdom.

chapters.label: Fifth Sabbath Song — Foundations of the holy dwelling
chapters.text: The song turns toward the structure of the heavenly sanctuary. Its foundations, chambers, and holy divisions are described in language of radiance and living glory. The building itself seems to participate in praise. [The surviving fragments are small.] The earthly worshipper is invited to imagine a sanctuary whose order exceeds ordinary architecture.

chapters.label: Sixth Sabbath Song — Seven chief princes
chapters.text: Seven chief princes are summoned to bless the King, and with them are corresponding priestly orders. One group blesses, another exalts, another gives thanks, and together they magnify the God of the holy ones. The repeated sevens shape the worship as a complete heavenly order rather than a solitary voice.

chapters.label: Seventh Sabbath Song — The heavenly temple
chapters.text: This central song dwells on the heavenly temple. Wonderful divine beings stand in its courts; engraved forms, living structures, and radiant spirits appear within the sanctuary. When the chief angels praise, the thresholds and foundations seem to respond. The vision joins architecture, beings, and sound into one act of worship before the divine throne.

chapters.label: Eighth Sabbath Song — Blessing in ordered ranks
chapters.text: The priestly spirits bless according to rank, each order answering the one above and below it. Their knowledge differs according to station, yet their praise is united. No jealousy breaks the harmony of the sanctuary. All glory returns to the God who established their offices and gives understanding to every holy spirit.

chapters.label: Ninth Sabbath Song — Garments and splendour
chapters.text: Fragments speak of priestly splendour, holy garments, and signs of rank. The heavenly ministers are clothed for service in a way that mirrors and surpasses earthly priesthood. Their adornment signifies office, purity, and glory rather than luxury. They stand ready for worship in the presence of the King.

chapters.label: Tenth Sabbath Song — The chariot throne
chapters.text: The vision intensifies around the divine throne and the chariot of glory. Living beings, wheels, and radiant forms appear in language related to prophetic throne visions. The sound of their movement joins the sound of praise. They do not praise themselves; their terrifying splendour directs attention to the One who sits above the heavenly assembly.

chapters.label: Eleventh Sabbath Song — Works of the living God
chapters.text: The holy beings recount the wondrous works of the living God and the mysteries of his wisdom. His knowledge orders both the heavenly sanctuary and the times of creation. The angels understand according to what has been revealed to them, and their response to revelation is blessing. [Several lines and transitions are lost.]

chapters.label: Twelfth Sabbath Song — Sacrifice of praise
chapters.text: The heavenly priesthood offers a sacrifice expressed above all in praise, blessing, and ordered service. The song uses priestly language without reducing heavenly worship to earthly animal sacrifice. The holy ones present the honour due to God's name, and the sanctuary resounds with their response.

chapters.label: Thirteenth Sabbath Song — Final exaltation
chapters.text: The final Sabbath song gathers the cycle toward exaltation. All priestly spirits, princes, councils, and holy beings bless the God of gods and the King of glory. His throne is above every order, and his holiness is beyond their holiness. [The ending survives only in fragments.] The cycle closes with the heavenly sanctuary still in worship, an unbroken liturgy before God.
